claims.text: Cascadia Public Employees' Retirement System ("CPERS") retained Vectera Advisors ("Vectera") as investment manager to invest and manage its real estate portfolio ("Portfolio" or "Program") in 2001. Vectera was awarded discretion over the Program beginning in 2011.

Cascadia Public Employees' Retirement System ("CPERS") retained Vectera Advisors ("Vectera") as investment manager
  to invest and manage its real estate portfolio ("Portfolio" or "Program") in 2001. Vectera was awarded discretion over the
 Program beginning in 2011.

claims.text: Since inception, $456.8M has been committed or approved for commitment across 14 individual investment positions: 12 funded and carried in the flash, plus 2 open approvals not funded by quarter-end. The funded investments have generated a since-inception net IRR of 9.3% and a 1.45x net equity multiple.
At quarter-end, portfolio NAV was $436.1M, or 8.8% of the $4,955.9M total plan and 88.0% of its $495.6M target real estate allocation.
The Portfolio returned 1.28% net during the quarter and 5.46% over one year, against 0.70% and 2.66%, respectively, for the CPERS Custom Benchmark.
The policy allocation to real estate is 10% of total plan assets, with an allowable range of 5-20%. The return objective is to exceed the CPERS Custom Benchmark.

claims.text: The Strategic sleeve represented 85.0% of portfolio market value and returned 1.16% net during the quarter.

Cornerstone Core Property Fund was the Portfolio's second-largest detractor and largest individual position. The Fund returned -0.34% net, with quarter-end NAV of $54.4M and 28.2% LTV. Income of $534,034.90, appreciation of -$557,954.40 and fees of $163,256.86 resulted in a -$187,176.36 dollar contribution.

Three assets shaped the quarter. One Financial Plaza (Chicago office) was written down on lower submarket comparables and a near-term lease expiry. Bayfront Apartments (San Diego) was held roughly flat as concessions offset rent growth. Prairie Logistics (Kansas City) contributed positively, partially offsetting the office drag. Leverage was conservative at ~28% LTV.

Kestrel U.S. Real Estate Fund. The Fund returned 1.66% net, with quarter-end NAV of $49.7M and 25.3% LTV.

Redwood Logistics Trust was the Portfolio's largest contributor and second-largest individual position. The Fund returned 2.69% net, with quarter-end NAV of $51.9M and 31.2% LTV. Income of $346,623.46, appreciation of $1,081,768.36 and fees of $61,356.27 resulted in a $1,367,035.55 dollar contribution.

Three assets drove the quarter. Gateway Logistics Center (Dallas) was marked up following the completion of lease-up to 97% occupancy at rents ahead of underwriting. Harbor 40 Distribution (Savannah) appreciated modestly on a new 10-year lease to an investment-grade tenant. Cedar Ridge Infill (Inland Empire) was held flat pending a planned expansion. Leverage remained conservative at approximately 31% loan-to-value.

claims.text: The previously approved $25.0M commitment to Alder Creek Multifamily Fund III was withdrawn during the quarter. The Fund closed at its hard cap without an allocation to the client.
The previously approved $30.0M commitment to Sentinel Logistics Income Fund lapsed during the quarter. The approval expired unexercised on 30 November 2025 and is not being renewed.

Core real-estate values are stabilizing after the 2023–2024 repricing; U.S. private funds have turned positive over the past year (see exhibits). We favor industrial / logistics and multifamily, remain underweight office, and are selective in retail. Leverage discipline and patient deployment into the recovery.

A resurgence in rate volatility could re-widen bid-ask spreads and stall the transaction recovery. Refinancing of 2020–2021 vintage debt at higher rates remains a sector-wide overhang, most acute in office. Slower-than-expected supply absorption in select multifamily submarkets.

Maintain leverage discipline; prefer moderate loan-to-value. Tilt toward industrial / logistics and multifamily; underweight office; be selective in retail. Deploy patiently into the recovery as pricing stabilizes.

value: Market Outlook — Fourth Quarter 2025
Vectera Advisors — House View
Key Themes
• Core real-estate values are stabilizing after the 2023–2024 repricing; U.S. private funds have turned positive over the past year (see exhibits).
• We favor industrial / logistics and multifamily, remain underweight office, and are selective in retail.
• Leverage discipline and patient deployment into the recovery.
Macro & Capital Markets
• Global macro is stabilizing; core values are recovering following the significant 2023–2024 repricing.
• U.S. private real estate fund returns have moved back into positive territory over the trailing year (exhibit).
• Cap rates have largely stabilized while the spread over Treasuries has widened, restoring the real-estate risk premium (exhibit).
• Transaction activity is rebounding from cyclical lows as rate volatility eases and bid-ask spreads narrow.
• We maintain leverage discipline and prefer moderate loan-to-value as financing normalizes.
Return Backdrop — U.S. Private Real Estate
Trailing 3-year returns still carry the drawdown, but the latest quarter and one-year figures have turned positive.

value: Industrial & Logistics — Overweight
• Our top overweight: fundamentals remain tight and rent growth is normalizing from double-digit peaks.
• Vacancy sits well below its long-run average; new supply is moderating after a record delivery wave.
• Focus on infill locations and outdoor / industrial storage.
Residential / Multifamily — Favored
• A widening own-versus-rent affordability gap supports durable rental demand (exhibit).
• Record new deliveries are peaking and set to taper, easing rent pressure.
• A key area of interest for new capital deployment.

value.title: U.S. Residential — Monthly Cost to Own vs. Rent

value: Office — Underweight
• Transaction cap rates have repriced sharply higher — well above appraisal marks (exhibit).
• A pronounced bifurcation persists; only best-in-class, well-located assets are favored.
• Leasing is improving off a low base, but the recovery is uneven.

value: Retail — Selective
• Years of minimal new supply against steady population growth have tightened availability, especially in the Sun Belt (exhibit).
• Grocery-anchored and necessity-based formats are favored for resilient cash flows.
• Discretionary and enclosed-mall formats remain out of favor.

value: Private Real Estate Debt — Opportunistic
• Reduced bank lending has widened spreads, creating selective opportunities in senior and mezzanine credit.
• Relevant for dedicated debt mandates; not a focus of core / value-add equity portfolios.
Risks We Are Monitoring
• A resurgence in rate volatility could re-widen bid-ask spreads and stall the transaction recovery.
• Refinancing of 2020–2021 vintage debt at higher rates remains a sector-wide overhang, most acute in office.
• Slower-than-expected supply absorption in select multifamily submarkets.
Positioning Summary
• Maintain leverage discipline; prefer moderate loan-to-value.
• Tilt toward industrial / logistics and multifamily; underweight office; be selective in retail.
• Deploy patiently into the recovery as pricing stabilizes.
